findings.title: A previously-working exemptions.toml waiver now crashes scans instead of running
findings.after:
for rule in rules_for_scan(id)
    rule == canonical && continue
    e = first(Ledger.entries(ledger, rule; scope = "policy"), 1)
    isempty(e) || throw(Ledger.LedgerError("$rule on $(e[1]["target"]) is a policy waiver of a rule $id enforces but does not own..."))
end — a policy waiver naming any rule a two-rule scan enforces OTHER than its catalogue-canonical one now throws instead of disabling the scan.
findings.why_it_matters: Any consumer's .gbg/exemptions.toml carrying `{id = "RULE.CIT.DOI", scope = "policy", target = "*"}` (or the RULE.CIT.NO_INACCESSIBLE / RULE.DOC.API_GROUPING equivalents on SCAN.DEAD_REF / SCAN.API_PAGE_STRUCTURE) was schema-valid and functionally accepted at base — it silently disabled the whole scan. After this change the identical file makes `gbg scan docs` raise an uncaught `Ledger.LedgerError`, which is caught nowhere between `run_scan` and `GBGCodingTools.main` (verified: only `Config.ConfigError` is special-cased in Main.jl's catch), so the CLI exits 3 ("crashed", with a backtrace) instead of the tool's own "cannot evaluate" (exit 2) convention used for the structurally identical case of a bad consumer config. `makedocs()` (the mandatory docs-build wrapper every consumer's docs/make.jl calls) is partly shielded because it runs `doctor(cfg, :QUICK)` first and CFG.EXEMPTIONS is in QUICK, so the failure surfaces as a doctor FAIL before `scan_docs` runs — but `doctor`'s own `check(...)` wrapper still raises an uncaught `ErrorException` out of `makedocs`, so the docs build still aborts uncleanly rather than through a documented exit code. No exemptions.toml migration, deprecation warning, or schema_version gate accompanies the change; a consumer only discovers the break when a scan or a build crashes (or when they proactively run `gbg doctor`).
findings.description: The underlying fix (a waiver of a scan's non-canonical rule should not silently disable the sibling rule's enforcement) closes a real, previously-documented defect and is thoroughly tested and cross-referenced in policy/RULES.toml and the new CFG.EXEMPTIONS doctor check. But the chosen mechanism — an uncaught `Ledger.LedgerError` thrown from deep inside the scan engine — routes a consumer-configuration mistake through the tool's generic crash path (exit 3, full backtrace) rather than through the exit-2 "cannot evaluate" path the diff itself is simultaneously formalizing for the structurally identical `Config.ConfigError` case in src/CLI/Main.jl. A config or ledger file that was accepted (if imperfectly honored) before this diff now aborts the process for a consumer who runs `gbg scan docs` directly, or whose CI does not run `gbg doctor` before the docs build.
findings.evidence: src/Scan.jl (head): "Two ledger entries are errors (`Ledger.LedgerError`), never silently void and never silently wide: an `arg_type` predicate on a text scan, and a `policy` entry on a rule the scan enforces that is NOT its canonical rule"; src/Scan.jl (base): "The mirror case is NOT fixed and is a known limit: a waiver on either rule still disables the WHOLE scan, so it withdraws enforcement of a sibling rule the consumer never exempted."

findings.title: `gbg round scripts` overhaul rejects the old invocation and can make historical round records unreadable
findings.before:
function refresh_scripts(cfg::AbstractDict, round::AbstractString; io::IO = stdout)
    dir, rec = guard(cfg, round; io)
    dst = Preflight.copy_scripts(cfg, String(rec["instrument"]), round)
    entry = Dict{String,Any}("at" => timestamp(), "head" => something(Git.head(cfg["root"]), "0"^40))
    ... — callable as `gbg round scripts <round>`, no flag required, and the schema's scripts_refreshed[] entry required only ["at", "head"].
findings.why_it_matters: Two distinct consumer-visible effects. (1) `gbg round scripts <round>` — a documented, previously-working invocation with no flags — now returns exit 2 unless a caller also supplies `--reason "…"` (≥24 chars); any script, alias or muscle-memory habit built on the old verb now fails outright. (2) Any `ROUND.toml` already on disk whose `scripts_refreshed` array was written by the base version of this same tool (2-field `{at, head}` entries — exactly what the pre-diff docstring says happened for round 2026-09-12-check-docs-01) becomes schema-invalid under the new required-field list. `RoundFiles.read_round` (unchanged by this diff) throws on schema-invalidity, and `Gate.gate_problems` (unchanged by this diff) treats ANY round directory with an unparseable ROUND.toml as fatal — `println(io, "gate: round directory $(r.name) has no valid ROUND.toml — exit 2"); fatal = true` — for every subsequent `gbg round *` verb and every `makedocs` docs build, not just the affected round. No migration of existing scripts_refreshed entries, and no schema_version bump, accompanies the new required fields.
findings.description: Recording why, when and which scripts were force-refreshed is a real improvement over an untraceable freeze-bypass, and the new CLI verb behavior is thoroughly documented (ARCHITECTURE.md D7/§6.2, policy/RULES.toml, policy/instruments.md) and tested for the forward-going case. What is not covered anywhere in the diff or its tests is the backward direction: a round record already on disk in the OLD (pre-diff) shape. Given `gate()` fails closed on any schema-invalid round under `.gbg/rounds/` — a pre-existing, otherwise reasonable design choice — tightening this one schema's required fields with no migration risks stalling the tool's own gate (hence every docs build and round verb) the first time it re-encounters a round refreshed under the prior tool version. I could not directly verify whether such a record is currently present (`.gbg/rounds/` is out of this lane's permitted scope), so I report the mechanism, not a confirmed live break.
findings.evidence: schema/round.schema.json before: "required": ["at", "head"]; after: "required": ["at", "head", "reason", "after_pass", "scripts"] on the same `additionalProperties: false` object. src/CLI/Gate.jl (unchanged): "if r.state in (:nomarker, :invalid) ... fatal = true; continue" runs over every round directory before any per-instrument filtering.
